19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	---
214	
215	## 七、投稿前通用准备
216	
217	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
218	
219	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
220	- **不要用**：
221	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
222	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
223	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
224	- 风险：
225	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
226	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
227	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
228	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
229	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
230	
231	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
232	
233	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
234	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
235	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
236	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
237	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
238	
239	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
240	
241	提交前必须逐一检查：
242	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
243	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
244	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
245	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
246	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
247	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
248	7. 所有专有名词有定义
249	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
250	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
251	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础
252

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进

- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度

- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"

- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？

- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

7	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
8	\label{sec:setup}
9	
10	\paragraph{Datasets.}
11	We train on 250 Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo} jailbreak conversations and 250 topic-anchored benign conversations, both generated via Qwen3-8B.
12	Topic anchoring ensures that benign conversations cover the same subject domains as jailbreak conversations and controls for topical confounds.
13	For out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation, we generate 80 Foot-in-the-Door (FITD)~\citep{fitd2024} and 80 Deceptive Delight (DD)~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} conversations through a separate pipeline with no overlap in attack templates or strategies with the training data.
14	The in-distribution (IID) test set consists of 76 held-out Crescendo conversations (38 jailbreak, 38 benign).
15	To assess adversarial robustness, we paraphrase the IID test set to produce 76 perturbed samples with mean BERTScore of 0.92 and lexical overlap of 0.20, confirming that surface forms change substantially while semantics are preserved.
16	
17	\paragraph{Baselines.}
18	We compare three detection methods.
19	\textbf{DisPeD} (ours): DeBERTa-v3-base~\citep{he2021deberta} fine-tuned with a multi-task objective combining 8-class persuasion strategy classification and binary jailbreak-intent classification (Section~\ref{sec:method}).
20	Turn-level [CLS] embeddings are aggregated via mean pooling for conversation-level binary classification.
21	\textbf{Vanilla DeBERTa}: the identical pipeline with an unfine-tuned DeBERTa encoder.
22	This baseline isolates the effect of persuasion-aware fine-tuning.
23	\textbf{TF-IDF LR}: TF-IDF features over full conversation text with logistic regression, serving as a lexical baseline.
24	We additionally evaluate LLM-as-judge baselines in Section~\ref{sec:llm_judge}.
25	
26	\paragraph{Metrics and implementation.}
27	We report F1 score for binary jailbreak detection at turn prefix lengths $K \in \{1, 2, 3, 5\}$ and on full conversations.
28	IID results report the mean and standard deviation across three random seeds (42, 123, 456); OOD results use seed 42.
29	Stage-1 fine-tuning uses a learning rate of $2 \times 10^{-5}$, batch size 16, and 10 epochs.
30	The multi-task loss weight $\lambda$ is set to 1.0.
31	The 8-class persuasion taxonomy is grounded in the Persuasion Attack Paradigm~\citep{zeng2024pap} and Cialdini's influence principles~\citep{cialdini2001influence}, with turn-level annotations produced by Qwen3-8B.
32	Stage-2 classification uses a two-layer MLP trained for 20 epochs over mean-pooled [CLS] embeddings.
33

72	Persuasion-aware fine-tuning enables robust detection of unseen attack types where vanilla semantic embeddings collapse.
73	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} presents F1 scores across three test conditions: IID Crescendo, OOD Deceptive Delight, and OOD FITD.
74	Figure~\ref{fig:cross_attack} provides a visual comparison at full conversation length.
75	
76	\paragraph{IID performance.}
77	All three methods achieve near-perfect F1 on in-distribution Crescendo test data.
78	TF-IDF LR reaches F1 = 1.000 at every prefix length, DisPeD achieves 0.996 or above, and Vanilla DeBERTa ranges from 0.944 to 1.000.
79	This ceiling effect reflects an inherent lexical separability between persuasive jailbreak and general benign conversations: even bag-of-words features suffice when the test distribution matches training.
80	The IID results establish a baseline expectation that any reasonable method can solve the in-distribution detection task, and confirm that persuasion-aware fine-tuning does not sacrifice in-distribution accuracy.
81	Vanilla DeBERTa's variance is highest at early prefixes ($K$=1: std=0.032, $K$=2: std=0.035), where fewer turns provide less signal for generic embeddings.
82	DisPeD reduces this variance to 0.008 across all $K$ values, reflecting more stable representations even with limited context.
83	
84	\paragraph{OOD: Deceptive Delight.}
85	The DD evaluation reveals the central finding of this paper.
86	Vanilla DeBERTa, the natural approach of encoding turns with a generic pretrained model, collapses to F1 = 0.284 on full DD conversations despite reaching 1.000 on IID data from the same pipeline.
87	The degradation worsens as more turns are observed: F1 drops from 0.575 at $K$=1 to 0.284 at Full.
88	This counterintuitive pattern is consistent with prior work showing that multi-turn attack turns are designed to remain in a ``benign'' embedding region~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}: each additional DD turn supplies more misleading ``benign'' evidence, pushing the model toward incorrect predictions rather than helping it detect the attack.
89	DisPeD maintains F1 $\geq$ 0.990 at every prefix length, including near-perfect early detection at $K$=1 (F1 = 1.000) and $K$=2 (F1 = 0.990).
90	The gap over Vanilla DeBERTa ranges from +42 pp at $K$=1 to +72 pp at Full.
91	Early detection is particularly important for deployment: at $K$=2, DisPeD detects attacks after just two turns (F1 = 0.990) while Vanilla DeBERTa has already dropped to 0.438.
92	
93	TF-IDF LR achieves F1 = 0.944 on full DD conversations, which confirms substantial lexical separability even across attack families.
94	We acknowledge this result openly: the primary contribution of DisPeD over TF-IDF is not raw detection performance but rather three complementary advantages.
95	First, DisPeD bridges the representation-level gap that vanilla semantic embeddings cannot (+72 pp on DD), validating persuasion-aware fine-tuning as the mechanism for cross-attack generalization.
96	Second, DisPeD achieves zero degradation under adversarial perturbation (Section~\ref{sec:perturbation}).
97	Third, DisPeD provides interpretable strategy trajectories for detection decisions (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}).
98	
99	\paragraph{OOD: FITD.}
100	FITD conversations are easier to detect across all methods.
101	DisPeD and Vanilla DeBERTa both reach F1 $\geq$ 0.990 at all evaluated prefixes, and TF-IDF LR achieves 1.000 on $K$=1 and full conversations.
102	The limited differentiation on FITD suggests this attack family shares more surface-level features with the Crescendo training data than DD does, reducing the cross-attack generalization challenge.

130	\paragraph{Label granularity.}

134	These results confirm that the encoder learns useful pragmatic features from exposure to persuasion-domain text during fine-tuning, regardless of whether strategy labels are correct, coarse, or random.
135	The finding parallels observations in domain-adaptive pretraining~\citep{gururangan2018artifacts}: the data domain matters more than the specific supervision signal.
136	In our setting, multi-task fine-tuning on persuasion-related conversations teaches the encoder to attend to pragmatic features (e.g., implicit requests, escalation cues, rapport-building patterns) that transfer across attack types.

206	Table~\ref{tab:llm_judge} reports zero-shot detection performance for GPT-5.5 and Qwen3-8B on the IID Crescendo test set, where both models are prompted to classify each conversation as jailbreak or benign.

208	GPT-5.5 achieves precision of 1.0 at all turn prefixes but recall ranges from only 0.105 to 0.290, resulting in F1 of 0.191 at $K$=2 and 0.449 at $K$=5.

216	Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo,li2024mhj}, and each turn maintains surface-level coherence with an innocuous cover topic.
217	An LLM analyzing conversation content sees a plausible discussion and lacks the pragmatic signal to recognize the underlying persuasion process.
218	DisPeD's learned persuasion features capture this pragmatic layer at a fraction of the inference cost of a frontier LLM, without requiring the conversation content to contain explicit harmful requests.

% experiments.tex — DisPeD Experiments Section
% Requires: booktabs, multirow, graphicx, multicolumn (standard)

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Datasets.}
We train on 250 Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo} jailbreak conversations and 250 topic-anchored benign conversations, both generated via Qwen3-8B.
Topic anchoring ensures that benign conversations cover the same subject domains as jailbreak conversations and controls for topical confounds.
For out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation, we generate 80 Foot-in-the-Door (FITD)~\citep{fitd2024} and 80 Deceptive Delight (DD)~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} conversations through a separate pipeline with no overlap in attack templates or strategies with the training data.
The in-distribution (IID) test set consists of 76 held-out Crescendo conversations (38 jailbreak, 38 benign).
To assess adversarial robustness, we paraphrase the IID test set to produce 76 perturbed samples with mean BERTScore of 0.92 and lexical overlap of 0.20, confirming that surface forms change substantially while semantics are preserved.

\paragraph{Baselines.}
We compare three detection methods.
\textbf{DisPeD} (ours): DeBERTa-v3-base~\citep{he2021deberta} fine-tuned with a multi-task objective combining 8-class persuasion strategy classification and binary jailbreak-intent classification (Section~\ref{sec:method}).
Turn-level [CLS] embeddings are aggregated via mean pooling for conversation-level binary classification.
\textbf{Vanilla DeBERTa}: the identical pipeline with an unfine-tuned DeBERTa encoder.
This baseline isolates the effect of persuasion-aware fine-tuning.
\textbf{TF-IDF LR}: TF-IDF features over full conversation text with logistic regression, serving as a lexical baseline.
We additionally evaluate LLM-as-judge baselines in Section~\ref{sec:llm_judge}.

\paragraph{Metrics and implementation.}
We report F1 score for binary jailbreak detection at turn prefix lengths $K \in \{1, 2, 3, 5\}$ and on full conversations.
IID results report the mean and standard deviation across three random seeds (42, 123, 456); OOD results use seed 42.
Stage-1 fine-tuning uses a learning rate of $2 \times 10^{-5}$, batch size 16, and 10 epochs.
The multi-task loss weight $\lambda$ is set to 1.0.
The 8-class persuasion taxonomy is grounded in the Persuasion Attack Paradigm~\citep{zeng2024pap} and Cialdini's influence principles~\citep{cialdini2001influence}, with turn-level annotations produced by Qwen3-8B.
Stage-2 classification uses a two-layer MLP trained for 20 epochs over mean-pooled [CLS] embeddings.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Cross-Attack Generalization}
\label{sec:cross_attack}

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-attack generalization (F1). All models trained on Crescendo conversations. IID results report 3-seed mean$\pm$std (seeds 42, 123, 456). OOD results use seed 42. $K$ denotes the number of conversation turns used for detection. Best per column per section in \textbf{bold}, second best \underline{underlined} (when three or more methods report values).}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & $K$=1 & $K$=2 & $K$=3 & $K$=5 & Full \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{IID (Crescendo)}} \\[2pt]
DisPeD (ours) & \underline{.996$\pm$.008} & \underline{.996$\pm$.008} & \underline{.996$\pm$.008} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} \\
Vanilla DeBERTa & .959$\pm$.032 & .944$\pm$.035 & .967$\pm$.019 & \underline{.982$\pm$.014} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} \\
TF-IDF LR & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} & \textbf{1.000$\pm$.000} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{OOD (Deceptive Delight)}} \\[2pt]
DisPeD (ours) & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{.990} & \textbf{.990} & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{1.000} \\
Vanilla DeBERTa & .575 & .438 & .360 & .311 & .284 \\
TF-IDF LR & -- & -- & -- & -- & \underline{.944} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{OOD (FITD)}} \\[2pt]
DisPeD (ours) & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{1.000} & -- & -- & \textbf{1.000} \\
Vanilla DeBERTa & \underline{.990} & \textbf{1.000} & -- & -- & \textbf{1.000} \\
TF-IDF LR & \textbf{1.000} & -- & -- & -- & \textbf{1.000} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig2_cross_attack_bar.pdf}
\caption{Cross-attack generalization at full conversation length. Vanilla DeBERTa collapses on unseen Deceptive Delight (F1 = 0.284) while DisPeD maintains F1 = 1.000. TF-IDF LR achieves 0.944 on DD, reflecting inherent lexical separability.}
\label{fig:cross_attack}
\end{figure}

Persuasion-aware fine-tuning enables robust detection of unseen attack types where vanilla semantic embeddings collapse.
Table~\ref{tab:main_results} presents F1 scores across three test conditions: IID Crescendo, OOD Deceptive Delight, and OOD FITD.
Figure~\ref{fig:cross_attack} provides a visual comparison at full conversation length.

\paragraph{IID performance.}
All three methods achieve near-perfect F1 on in-distribution Crescendo test data.
TF-IDF LR reaches F1 = 1.000 at every prefix length, DisPeD achieves 0.996 or above, and Vanilla DeBERTa ranges from 0.944 to 1.000.
This ceiling effect reflects an inherent lexical separability between persuasive jailbreak and general benign conversations: even bag-of-words features suffice when the test distribution matches training.
The IID results establish a baseline expectation that any reasonable method can solve the in-distribution detection task, and confirm that persuasion-aware fine-tuning does not sacrifice in-distribution accuracy.
Vanilla DeBERTa's variance is highest at early prefixes ($K$=1: std=0.032, $K$=2: std=0.035), where fewer turns provide less signal for generic embeddings.
DisPeD reduces this variance to 0.008 across all $K$ values, reflecting more stable representations even with limited context.

\paragraph{OOD: Deceptive Delight.}
The DD evaluation reveals the central finding of this paper.
Vanilla DeBERTa, the natural approach of encoding turns with a generic pretrained model, collapses to F1 = 0.284 on full DD conversations despite reaching 1.000 on IID data from the same pipeline.
The degradation worsens as more turns are observed: F1 drops from 0.575 at $K$=1 to 0.284 at Full.
This counterintuitive pattern is consistent with prior work showing that multi-turn attack turns are designed to remain in a ``benign'' embedding region~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}: each additional DD turn supplies more misleading ``benign'' evidence, pushing the model toward incorrect predictions rather than helping it detect the attack.
DisPeD maintains F1 $\geq$ 0.990 at every prefix length, including near-perfect early detection at $K$=1 (F1 = 1.000) and $K$=2 (F1 = 0.990).
The gap over Vanilla DeBERTa ranges from +42 pp at $K$=1 to +72 pp at Full.
Early detection is particularly important for deployment: at $K$=2, DisPeD detects attacks after just two turns (F1 = 0.990) while Vanilla DeBERTa has already dropped to 0.438.

TF-IDF LR achieves F1 = 0.944 on full DD conversations, which confirms substantial lexical separability even across attack families.
We acknowledge this result openly: the primary contribution of DisPeD over TF-IDF is not raw detection performance but rather three complementary advantages.
First, DisPeD bridges the representation-level gap that vanilla semantic embeddings cannot (+72 pp on DD), validating persuasion-aware fine-tuning as the mechanism for cross-attack generalization.
Second, DisPeD achieves zero degradation under adversarial perturbation (Section~\ref{sec:perturbation}).
Third, DisPeD provides interpretable strategy trajectories for detection decisions (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}).

\paragraph{OOD: FITD.}
FITD conversations are easier to detect across all methods.
DisPeD and Vanilla DeBERTa both reach F1 $\geq$ 0.990 at all evaluated prefixes, and TF-IDF LR achieves 1.000 on $K$=1 and full conversations.
The limited differentiation on FITD suggests this attack family shares more surface-level features with the Crescendo training data than DD does, reducing the cross-attack generalization challenge.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Ablation Study}
\label{sec:ablation}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Ablation study on OOD Deceptive Delight and IID. All variants trained on Crescendo. The persuasion fine-tuning process is the critical factor; label granularity and temporal modeling are not.}
\label{tab:ablation}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Variant} & DD-Full & DD-$K$=2 & IID-Full \\
\midrule
DisPeD (8-class) & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{.990} & 1.000 \\
Scrambled labels & .990 & .981 & 1.000 \\
Binary (2-class) & .990 & .981 & 1.000 \\
GRU aggregation & .990 & \textbf{.990} & 1.000 \\
\midrule
Vanilla DeBERTa & .284 & .438 & 1.000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The fine-tuning process on persuasion-related text, not specific label assignments, is what drives cross-attack generalization.
Table~\ref{tab:ablation} reports DD-OOD and IID F1 for several model variants, grouped into fine-tuned variants (above the mid-rule) and the unfine-tuned baseline (below).

\paragraph{Label granularity.}
Replacing the 8-class persuasion taxonomy with randomly scrambled labels reduces DD-Full F1 from 1.000 to 0.990, a gap of just 1 pp.
Collapsing the taxonomy to binary (persuasion-present vs.\ absent) yields the same 0.990.
Both variants remain far above the vanilla baseline (F1 = 0.284), a gap exceeding 70 pp.
These results confirm that the encoder learns useful pragmatic features from exposure to persuasion-domain text during fine-tuning, regardless of whether strategy labels are correct, coarse, or random.
The finding parallels observations in domain-adaptive pretraining~\citep{gururangan2018artifacts}: the data domain matters more than the specific supervision signal.
In our setting, multi-task fine-tuning on persuasion-related conversations teaches the encoder to attend to pragmatic features (e.g., implicit requests, escalation cues, rapport-building patterns) that transfer across attack types.
The 8-class taxonomy provides interpretability through strategy trajectory analysis (Section~\ref{sec:strategy}) rather than a detection advantage over coarser alternatives.
From a practical standpoint, this result lowers the annotation barrier: coarse or imperfect persuasion labels suffice for training an effective cross-attack detector.

\paragraph{Temporal modeling.}
Replacing mean pooling with a GRU over the [CLS] sequence yields DD-Full F1 = 0.990, within 1 pp of the mean-pooling default (1.000).
This equivalence confirms that the model detects persuasion presence in individual turns rather than relying on the temporal ordering of strategies across the conversation.
Mean pooling is the default in all other experiments.

\paragraph{Fine-tuning as the critical factor.}
The most informative comparison spans all ablation rows.
Every variant that includes persuasion-domain fine-tuning achieves DD-Full F1 $\geq$ 0.990, while Vanilla DeBERTa collapses to 0.284.
All fine-tuned variants also maintain IID-Full F1 = 1.000.
This 70+ pp gap on OOD data establishes that persuasion-aware fine-tuning is both necessary and sufficient for cross-attack generalization; architecture choices and label granularity are secondary factors.
We also evaluated a $\lambda=0$ variant (intent classification only, no persuasion task), which achieves IID-Full F1 = 1.000. OOD evaluation was not conducted for this variant, but the IID result confirms that the intent head alone suffices for in-distribution detection. The persuasion task is specifically needed for OOD generalization.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Robustness Under Adversarial Perturbation}
\label{sec:perturbation}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Robustness under adversarial paraphrasing (IID test set, full conversations). Perturbed set preserves semantics (BERTScore 0.92) while altering surface forms (lexical overlap 0.20). $\Delta$: degradation in percentage points.}
\label{tab:perturbation}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & Original & Perturbed & $\Delta$ (pp) \\
\midrule
DisPeD (ours) & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{0.0} \\
Vanilla DeBERTa & 1.000 & .882 & $-$11.8 \\
TF-IDF LR & 1.000 & \underline{.987} & \underline{$-$1.3} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

DisPeD maintains perfect detection under adversarial paraphrasing while both baselines degrade.
Table~\ref{tab:perturbation} reports F1 on the original and perturbed IID test sets (76 samples each).
The perturbed set was constructed via automated paraphrasing that preserves semantic content (BERTScore 0.92) while substantially altering surface forms (lexical overlap 0.20).

DisPeD achieves F1 = 1.000 on both original and perturbed data, with zero degradation.
Vanilla DeBERTa drops from 1.000 to 0.882, a loss of 11.8 pp, consistent with its reliance on surface-level features from the unfine-tuned encoder.
TF-IDF LR shows a smaller but measurable decline from 1.000 to 0.987 (1.3 pp).
The ordering follows the expected robustness hierarchy: features learned through persuasion-aware fine-tuning capture pragmatic patterns that are invariant to surface rephrasing, while generic embeddings and lexical features are more sensitive to word-level changes.
Combined with the cross-attack results in Table~\ref{tab:main_results}, the perturbation evaluation confirms that persuasion-aware fine-tuning produces representations robust to both unseen attack types and adversarial surface variation.
The zero-degradation result is particularly relevant for deployment scenarios where attackers may attempt to evade detection through paraphrasing or style transfer~\citep{nasr2025attackermovessecond}.
While our perturbation evaluation uses automated paraphrasing rather than adversary-crafted evasion, the 11.8 pp degradation of Vanilla DeBERTa under even this moderate perturbation suggests that unfine-tuned representations would be fragile against more targeted adaptive attacks.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{LLM-as-Judge Baseline}
\label{sec:llm_judge}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{LLM-as-judge zero-shot Crescendo detection (IID test set). F1 values exclude unparseable responses and therefore represent upper bounds.$^{\dagger}$Unparseable rate increases with context length: 30\% at $K$=2 to 47\% at Full.}
\label{tab:llm_judge}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & $K$=2 & $K$=3 & $K$=5 & Full & Unparse. \\
\midrule
GPT-5.5 & .191 & .273 & .449 & .383 & 30--47\%$^{\dagger}$ \\
Qwen3-8B & .000 & .051 & .146 & .100 & 0\% \\
\midrule
DisPeD (ours) & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{1.000} & \textbf{1.000} & 0\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Frontier language models fail at multi-turn jailbreak detection even when given full conversation context.
Table~\ref{tab:llm_judge} reports zero-shot detection performance for GPT-5.5 and Qwen3-8B on the IID Crescendo test set, where both models are prompted to classify each conversation as jailbreak or benign.

GPT-5.5 achieves precision of 1.0 at all turn prefixes but recall ranges from only 0.105 to 0.290, resulting in F1 of 0.191 at $K$=2 and 0.449 at $K$=5.
A substantial fraction of GPT-5.5 responses are unparseable: the rate increases from 30\% at $K$=2 to 47\% on full conversations.
The F1 values in Table~\ref{tab:llm_judge} exclude unparseable responses and therefore represent upper bounds on actual performance.
Full-conversation F1 (0.383) is lower than $K$=5 F1 (0.449) because the unparseable rate grows with context length, not because the model classifies worse on parsed responses.
The high precision but low recall pattern suggests that GPT-5.5 is deceived by Crescendo's surface educational framing: when the model does commit to a classification, it correctly identifies jailbreaks, but the majority of attacks go undetected.

Qwen3-8B performs worse across all prefixes, with F1 from 0.000 at $K$=2 to 0.100 on full conversations, and produces no unparseable responses.
The failure of both a frontier commercial model and an open-weight model highlights a fundamental limitation of content-level reasoning for this task.
Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo,li2024mhj}, and each turn maintains surface-level coherence with an innocuous cover topic.
An LLM analyzing conversation content sees a plausible discussion and lacks the pragmatic signal to recognize the underlying persuasion process.
DisPeD's learned persuasion features capture this pragmatic layer at a fraction of the inference cost of a frontier LLM, without requiring the conversation content to contain explicit harmful requests.

%----------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Strategy Trajectory Analysis}
\label{sec:strategy}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/paper/fig3_strategy_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{Persuasion strategy transition matrices for three attack types. Left: Crescendo (1,818 transitions, all 8 strategies). Middle: FITD (541 transitions, 4 strategies). Right: DD (565 transitions, 6 strategies). Each cell shows transition probability from the row strategy to the column strategy. Attack types exhibit distinct escalation patterns that DisPeD can expose for human inspection.}
\label{fig:strategy_heatmap}
\end{figure*}

Different multi-turn attack types produce distinct persuasion strategy trajectories that provide native interpretability for detection decisions.
Figure~\ref{fig:strategy_heatmap} visualizes strategy transition matrices for Crescendo, FITD, and DD, computed from the 8-class persuasion labels predicted by DisPeD's fine-tuned encoder.

Crescendo conversations exhibit gradual escalation across all 8 strategy types, with the mean strategy index increasing from 0.86 in early turns to 5.64 in later turns across 1,818 total transitions.
This steady progression reflects Crescendo's design: each turn incrementally shifts toward more aggressive persuasion while maintaining plausible deniability at every individual step.

FITD conversations employ a narrower repertoire of 4 strategies (Rapport Building, Authority Appeal, Logical Appeal, Escalation) across 541 transitions.
The foot-in-the-door structure produces a commitment-then-escalation pattern: early turns secure agreement on mild requests before the attacker increases demands.

DD conversations use 6 of the 8 strategies across 565 transitions, with characteristic emotional manipulation and role-assignment sequences that are distinct from both Crescendo and FITD patterns.
The broader strategy repertoire in DD (6 strategies vs.\ 4 in FITD) is consistent with its hybrid design, which combines distraction through benign topics with embedded harmful requests~\citep{deceptivedelight2024}.

These trajectory signatures serve two purposes.
For practitioners, they provide human-interpretable explanations for detection decisions: a security analyst can inspect the predicted strategy sequence to understand why a conversation was flagged.
For the research question, the diversity of trajectories across attack families confirms that persuasion-aware fine-tuning captures generalizable pragmatic structure rather than memorizing surface patterns from a single attack type.
We emphasize that strategy trajectories are an interpretability contribution, not a detection mechanism: the ablation in Section~\ref{sec:ablation} shows that mean pooling (which discards turn order) matches GRU performance, so DisPeD detects persuasion presence per turn rather than relying on temporal trajectory patterns.
